core_concepts: Delays complicate systems because causes and effects are separated in time
A delayed system can make a good policy look ineffective in the short run
The author argues that delay awareness changes how performance should be read
Delays Delays complicate systems because causes and effects are separated in time
When feedback is delayed, decision makers often overreact to the latest signal and create oscillation instead of control
Suppose inventory orders are increased today, but shipments will not arrive for 6 weeks
It is not enough to ask whether a policy worked; the analyst must also ask when the system could reasonably reveal that it worked
In volatile settings, the combination of strong feedback and long delays is especially dangerous because it rewards urgency while punishing patience
Why delays mislead A delayed system can make a good policy look ineffective in the short run
